key_idea: Recast p_c<p_u as an operator-norm statement p_c<p_{2→2} for the two-point matrix T_p, which via Cheeger's inequality reduces to showing the two-point matrix has vanishing 'isoperimetric' mass on finite sets near p_c; this is established with a hyperbolic Magic Lemma (Bonk–Schramm embedding plus Benjamini–Schramm Magic Lemma) and a mean-field susceptibility bound from half-space disjointness.
reason: The operator-theoretic reduction (Corollary 12, Lemma 14 via Cheeger, Riesz–Thorin) is a striking and reusable framework, and the conclusion follows cleanly once Propositions 33 and 34 are known. But those propositions rest on a long geometric apparatus: the Bonk–Schramm embedding, a classification of boundary actions, a comparison of discrete and continuum half-spaces, non-degeneracy lemmas, a new Magic Lemma, and separate nonunimodular and unimodular cases. So the elegant core is buried under substantial technical machinery.
recognized: Hutchcroft, 'Non-uniqueness and mean-field criticality for percolation on nonamenable Cayley graphs / hyperbolic graphs' (Percolation on hyperbolic graphs, GAFA 2019)
